grades.quote: The system call path adds four to the saved user program counter because RISC-V, in the case of a system call, leaves the program pointer pointing to the ecall instruction but user code needs to resume executing at the subsequent instruction.
grades.reason: Shows how xv6 uses the saved program counter (sepc) after a trap. It saves sepc, adds 4 after an ecall system call so execution resumes at the next instruction, restores sepc, and returns with sret. It does not describe the hardware saving step in detail.

grades.quote: sepc: When a trap occurs, RISC-V saves the program counter here (since the pc is then overwritten with the value in stvec). The sret (return from trap) instruction copies sepc to the pc. The kernel can write sepc to control where sret goes.
grades.reason: Directly explains that on a trap RISC-V copies the pc into sepc, that sret copies sepc back to the pc, and that the kernel can write sepc to control where sret goes. It also lists the hardware trap steps.
